info.title: VictorOps API — baton-victorops connector surface
info.description: This document covers ONLY the VictorOps / Splunk On-Call REST API operations that the baton-victorops connector (pkg/connector/client) actually calls. It is not a full mirror of the vendor's public API. Shapes are derived from pkg/connector/client/*.go (which endpoints and fields the connector depends on) and settled against the vendor's officially published Swagger 2.0 document at https://portal.victorops.com/public/api-docs/victorops-api-v1.yaml (vendor spec version 0.0.3, fetched live 2026-10-01). See the accompanying PR description for a full provenance table and a list of discrepancies found between the connector's implementation and the vendor's documented contract.

servers.description: Default VictorOps API base URL (pkg/connector/client/client.go DefaultBaseURL). Overridable via the connector's hidden `base-url` config field / `--base-url` CLI flag (pkg/config/config.go BaseURLField), which exists for testing against a mock server and is not meant for production use.

get.description:
Get a list of users for the organization. Client: pkg/connector/client/users.go:8 (ListUsers), called from pkg/connector/users.go. No pagination parameters are sent or supported by this endpoint — the vendor spec and docs confirm this returns the full org user list in one response.

ANOMALY (see PR blockers): the connector decodes the `users` field into a Go `[][]User` (array of arrays), while the vendor spec documents `users` as a flat array of user objects (matching ListTeamResponse's sibling shapes). This schema models the vendor-documented flat array; the connector's nested-array Go type appears to be a latent bug and is flagged separately rather than encoded here.

200.description: A list of users for the organization

422.description: You have reached your user limit.

get.description: Get a list of teams for the organization. Client: pkg/connector/client/team.go:9 (ListTeams), called from pkg/connector/team.go. No pagination parameters are sent or supported — the vendor spec documents this as returning the full list in one response, and the connector decodes it directly as a flat array (`[]Team`), matching the vendor's un-wrapped array response.

200.description: A list of teams for the organization

422.description: You have reached your team limit.

get.summary: Retrieve a list of members for a team
get.description:
Client: pkg/connector/client/team.go:22 (ListTeamMembers), called from pkg/connector/team.go Grants(). No pagination.

CONNECTOR BUG (see PR blockers): pkg/connector/client/team.go:39 (ListTeamAdmins) also issues a GET request to this exact same path (it uses the `TeamMembersEndpoint` constant instead of the unused `TeamAdminsEndpoint` constant, which points at `/api-public/v1/team/{team}/admins`). ListTeamAdmins then tries to decode a `teamAdmins` field from this response, which this endpoint never returns (only `members`), so ListTeamAdmins always yields an empty slice in production. The vendor-documented `/api-public/v1/team/{team}/admins` endpoint is never actually called by the connector and is therefore NOT included in this spec's scope.

200.description: A list of members for the team

422.description: Team name or email is unavailable, or you have reached your team limit.

post.description: Adds a user to a team. Client: pkg/connector/client/team.go:56 (AddUserTeam), called from pkg/connector/team.go Grant() when granting the team `member` entitlement. The connector sends only `username` in the JSON body and discards the response body (passes a nil response target), so the 200 schema below is documented from the vendor spec but not consumed by the connector.

200.description: Some details about the team that was added (response body is not parsed by the connector)

422.description: Team name or email is unavailable, or you have reached your team limit.

delete.description:
Removes a user from a team. Client: pkg/connector/client/team.go:75 (RemoveUserTeam), called from pkg/connector/team.go Revoke().

DISCREPANCY (see PR blockers): the vendor spec marks the request body's `replacement` field as required (a replacement username to take over any on-call duties held by the removed member). The connector sends an empty JSON object `{}` and never supplies `replacement`. This schema documents the vendor's required contract; it does not reflect what the connector actually transmits.

requestBody.description: Per the vendor spec this body is required with a required `replacement` field. The connector itself sends `{}` (see description above).

422.description: There was a problem with the delete such as the replacement team member was not found.

get.description:
Get all on-call users/teams for the organization. Client: pkg/connector/client/team.go:89 (ListCurrentOnCallTeamsWithUsers), called from pkg/connector/oncall_schedule.go List().

NOTE: the connector decodes the nested `team` object using its full `Team` struct (same type used by GET /api-public/v1/team), but the vendor spec documents this endpoint's nested team object (`OnCallTeamResource`) as containing only `name` and `slug`. The connector only reads `team.Slug` from this response in practice (see pkg/connector/oncall_schedule.go), so the extra fields being absent here does not break the connector, but the other `Team` fields will always be empty when populated from this endpoint. This schema models the vendor-documented minimal shape.

200.description: All users and escalation policies currently on call

VOApiId.name: X-VO-Api-Id
VOApiId.description: VictorOps API ID. Set via BATON_VICTOROPS_API_ID / --victorops-api-id. Both this and VOApiKey are required on every request (pkg/connector/client/client.go request()).

VOApiKey.name: X-VO-Api-Key
VOApiKey.description: VictorOps API key. Set via BATON_VICTOROPS_API_KEY / --victorops-api-key. A read-only key cannot perform the provisioning writes (addTeamMember / removeTeamMember) per the connector README.

BadRequest.description: Problem with the request arguments. The response payload may include an error message.

User.description: Vendor: V1User. Source fields: pkg/connector/client/models.go User struct.

username.description: Immutable; used as the connector's resource ID / join key for team membership and on-call grants.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp per vendor docs; typed as a plain string, format not documented by the vendor.

verified.description: Whether or not this user has set their password (per vendor docs, will always be false).

Team.description: Vendor: TeamDetail. Source fields: pkg/connector/client/models.go Team struct.

slug.description: Used by the connector as the team resource ID.

description.description: Read by the connector (team.go profile field) but NOT present in the vendor's published TeamDetail schema — unproven/client-code-only field, see PR blockers.

verified.description: Vendor spec types this field as `string` with description 'will always be false', which is inconsistent with its own sibling User.verified (documented as boolean) and with the connector's Go type (bool). Modeled here as boolean; flagged as a vendor-doc inconsistency in the PR, not guessed.

AddTeamMemberPayload.description: Vendor: AddTeamMemberPayload. Matches client.go team.go:57 Body{Username} exactly.

RemoveTeamMemberPayload.description: Vendor: RemoveTeamMemberPayload. NOTE: the connector sends `{}` and never populates `replacement` — see the operation description and PR blockers.

replacement.description: Username of the team member who should take over any on-call duties held by the removed member.

OnCallTeamRef.description: Vendor: OnCallTeamResource — the minimal team shape actually returned inside the on-call response. The connector decodes this into its full `Team` Go struct, so fields other than `name`/`slug` will always be empty when sourced from this endpoint.
